# Core library: catalogue

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_catalogue.py from the code; do not edit by hand. -->

The framework every application builds on: the network, the layers, the model, the set-up helpers, and the general-purpose constitutive laws and drives.
Every application is set up the same way; see [Using noodl](../usage.md).

Import from `noodl.topology` and the modules named in each table. The full reference, with every parameter, is in the [API reference](../api.md).

## Set-up

Build the model and its starting state and inputs.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `drivers_from`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | A drivers dictionary from `{key: {label: value}}` and/or `{key: tensor}`. | `drivers_from(model, values, *, base=None)` |
| `state_from`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | A state dictionary, as `drivers_from` builds drivers. | `state_from(model, values, *, base=None)` |
| `initial_drivers`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | A copy of the model's driver template (`model.driver_template`, which an application's `build_model` records), then `values` (see `drivers_from`). | `initial_drivers(model, *, values=None)` |
| `check_setup`<br><small>`noodl.validation`</small> | Check `model` and, when given, `state` and `drivers`; return a `SetupReport`. | `check_setup(model, state=None, drivers=None, *, dt=None, probe=False, steady=False, names=None)` |

## Layers and model

The conservation layers and the model that steps them.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `Network`<br><small>`noodl.topology`</small> | Directed multigraph with typed edges and tensor-valued topology operators. | `Network(dtype=torch.float32)` |
| `Ports`<br><small>`noodl.model`</small> | What a coupled or external model may prescribe and read. | `Ports(boundary_nodes, prescribed_keys, boundary_flows, flow_keys=<factory>)` |
| `Model`<br><small>`noodl.model`</small> | Layers on one `Network`, stepped together. See the module docstring for the keys. | `Model(net, layers, closures=(), reactions=(), coupling='pingpong', iterate_tol=None, iterate_max=20, substeps=None, adjoint_rtol=1e-10, iterate_relaxation=0.5, reaction_order='after_transport', iterate_acceleration=None, iterate_memory=5, iterate_flow_tol=None, iterate_on_limit='raise')` |
| `AllocatedFlowLayer`<br><small>also `CapacitatedTransferLayer`</small><br><small>`noodl.layers`</small> | Flows allocated by rule, not by a potential: each edge's requested flow is clipped to the arc's capacity and the receiving node's free storage, one explicit step at a time, conserving storage exactly (WSIMOD's push/pull semantics). `quantity`, `unit` and `flow_unit` are reported by `model.refs`, never used numerically. | `AllocatedFlowLayer(net, name, kind, *, s_max, c_arc, preference=None, mode='hard', tau=None, n_passes=5, quantity='storage', unit='', flow_unit='')` |
| `KirchhoffLayer`<br><small>`noodl.layers`</small> | Flows driven by a potential (pressure, head): solves nodal conservation `A_I g(A^T phi) = s_I` for the interior potentials by Newton's method, with the constitutive laws on its edge kinds, drives added to the potential differences, and prescribed potentials at its boundary nodes; differentiable through the converged solution. `flow_unit` is reported by `model.refs`, never used numerically. | `KirchhoffLayer(net, name, laws, drives=(), boundary=(), linear_solver='auto', *, node_sources=(), quantity='potential', unit='', flow_unit='', phasor=False, analytic_primal=False, newton_defaults=None)` |
| `TransportLayer`<br><small>`noodl.layers`</small> | dx/dt = M x + N x_b + sources / capacity on this layer's ACTIVE interior nodes. | `TransportLayer(net, name, *, capacity, flow_kind, boundary, n_species=1, carrier=1.0, transmission=None, kinetics=None, removal=None, conduction_kind=None, conductance=None, dilution=None, storage_free=(), scheme='exact', linear_solver='auto', quantity='scalar', unit='', species_names=None, source_unit='', capacity_unit='', flow_unit='')` |
| `CoupledModel`<br><small>`noodl.couple`</small> | Returned by `union`. `.step` takes and returns `{model_tag: State}` / `{model_tag: Drivers}` -- each model keeps its own dicts; nothing is merged. | `CoupledModel(models, links, aliases, substeps, *, relaxation=0.5, iterate_rtol=1e-08, iterate_atol=0.0, iterate_max=50, adjoint_rtol=1e-10)` |

## Constitutive laws

The relation between the flow through an edge and the potential difference across it.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `AffinityFan`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | A fan curve run at another speed and air density, by the fan laws (ContamX's performance-curve fan, measured against ContamX 3.4.1.7). | `AffinityFan(curve, *, src, tgt, rho_ref, speed_key=None, off=0.0, multiplier=1.0, shutoff=None, rho_key='rho', kind=None)` |
| `AirDuct`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | A duct segment, F (kg/s) from dp (Pa): Darcy-Weisbach with ContamX's friction factor. | `AirDuct(length, diameter, roughness, loss=0.0, *, area=None, src, tgt, rho_key='rho', temperature_key=None, kind='duct', learnable=False)` |
| `Conductance`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | q = g dp, the linear branch law used for thermal conduction and passive exchange; `g` is in the flow unit per unit of potential (W/K for heat, kg/s per Pa for air). | `Conductance(g, *, kind='conduction', learnable=False)` |
| `CubicSplineFlow`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | An airflow element given by measured points, fitted as ContamX fits them (`SplineCurve`): CONTAM's cubic-spline elements. | `CubicSplineFlow(x, y, *, independent='pressure', volume=False, multiplier=1.0, src, tgt, rho_key='rho', kind='airpath')` |
| `Damper`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Separate power-law coefficient and exponent for each flow direction: `C_pos`/`n_pos` for dp > 0 and `C_neg`/`n_neg` for dp < 0, each as in `PowerLaw` (`C` in the flow unit per Pa^n, `n` dimensionless). | `Damper(C_pos, n_pos, C_neg, n_neg, *, dp_transition=0.001, src=None, tgt=None, m=0.0, rho_ref=1.2041, rho_key='rho', kind='damper', learnable=False)` |
| `DoorCompartment`<br><small>also `MBLDoorCompartment`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | One compartment of ``Buildings.Airflow.Multizone.DoorDiscretizedOpen`` per edge. | `DoorCompartment(*, src, tgt, medium, dA, CD=0.65, m=0.5, dp_turbulent=0.01, vZer=0.001, T_key='T', Xw_key='X_w', p_key='p_abs', kind='door', learnable=False)` |
| `DoorPortStream`<br><small>also `MBLDoorPortStream`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | One of the two port streams of a whole discretised door, as ONE edge from side A to side B: ``direction="ab"`` returns ``port_a1.m_flow = mAB_flow``, ``"ba"`` returns ``port_b2.m_flow = -port_a2.m_flow = -mBA_flow`` (kg/s, both positive from A to B), from the compartment law ``comp`` (:class:`DoorCompartment` or :class:`OperableDoorCompartment`, one door) at the compartment pressure differences ``dp + head(drivers)`` (:class:`DoorCompartmentHead`). The edge's own ``dp`` is the zones' potential difference ``phi_A - phi_B``. | `DoorPortStream(comp, head, direction, kind)` |
| `Duct`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Colebrook duct: F(dp) with friction from the Colebrook equation, laminar below Re_t. Length `L`, diameter `D` and roughness `eps` (m); `sum_C` the dimensionless sum of dynamic loss coefficients; `A` (m2) defaults to the circular area; `rho` (kg/m3) and `mu` (Pa s); the flow is a mass flow in kg/s. | `Duct(L, D, eps, sum_C=0.0, *, A=None, Re_t=2000.0, rho=1.2041, mu=1.81625e-05, n_iter=4, kind='duct', learnable=False)` |
| `DuctTerminal`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | A duct terminal, the zero-length duct between a junction and its zone, F (kg/s) from dp (Pa), as ContamX 3.4.1.7 computes it (measured). | `DuctTerminal(area, loss, *, src, tgt, rho_key='rho', temperature_key=None, opening_key=None, kind='duct_terminal', learnable=False)` |
| `FanCurve`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Cubic pressure-flow curve inverted for q given dp on [0, q_max]: `coeffs` are (a0, a1, a2, a3) of P(q) = a0 + a1 q + a2 q^2 + a3 q^3 in Pa for q in the flow unit, and `q_max` is the largest flow the curve covers, in that unit. | `FanCurve(coeffs, q_max, *, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `FixedFlow`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | q = q0 regardless of dp (`q0` in the flow unit); dflow = 0; linear_init = (q0, 0). | `FixedFlow(q0, *, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `FixedVolumeFlow`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | F = Q rho_up whatever dp: a constant volume flow `volume_flow` Q (m3/s, one per edge) delivered as mass flow at the density of the node it draws from (`src` when Q >= 0, `tgt` otherwise), read from `drivers[rho_key]` (full node order). ContamX's constant-volume fan in a duct (measured). | `FixedVolumeFlow(volume_flow, *, src, tgt, rho_key='rho', kind='fan', learnable=False)` |
| `OpenDoor`<br><small>also `MBLDoorOpen`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | ``Buildings.Airflow.Multizone.DoorOpen``: one direction of the always-open door. | `OpenDoor(*, direction, src, tgt, medium, wOpe=0.9, hOpe=2.1, CD=0.65, m=0.5, dp_turbulent=0.01, T_key='T', kind='door', learnable=False)` |
| `OperableDoor`<br><small>also `MBLDoorOperable`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | ``Buildings.Airflow.Multizone.DoorOperable``: the door blended between open and closed by the opening signal ``y`` read from ``drivers[y_key]``. | `OperableDoor(*, direction, src, tgt, medium, y_key, LClo, wOpe=0.9, hOpe=2.1, CDOpe=0.65, mOpe=0.5, mClo=0.65, dpCloRat=4.0, CDCloRat=1.0, dp_turbulent=0.01, T_key='T', kind='door', learnable=False)` |
| `OperableDoorCompartment`<br><small>also `MBLDoorCompartmentOperable`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | One compartment of ``Buildings.Airflow.Multizone.DoorDiscretizedOperable`` per edge, blended between the open door and the closed crack by ``y = drivers[y_key]``. | `OperableDoorCompartment(*, src, tgt, medium, y_key, AOpe, LClo, nCom, CDOpe=0.65, CDClo=0.65, CDCloRat=1.0, dpCloRat=4.0, mOpe=0.5, mClo=0.65, dp_turbulent=0.01, vZer=0.001, T_key='T', Xw_key='X_w', p_key='p_abs', kind='door', learnable=False)` |
| `PowerLaw`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | q = C sign(dp) \|dp\|^n, laminar-blended or smoothly regularised near dp = 0. `dp` is in Pa; `C` is in the flow unit per Pa^n (kg/s for a mass-flow coefficient, m3/s for a volume-flow one), so the flow comes out in whatever unit `C` carries; `n` is dimensionless (0.5 for an orifice, towards 1 for a laminar crack). | `PowerLaw(C, n, *, dp_transition=0.001, regularised=None, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `PrescribedFlow`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | F = drivers[key] whatever dp: a flow (kg/s, one value per edge of the kind) that a closure or an input prescribes every step, e.g. an air handler's supply flows. `dtype` is the layer's: `linear_init`, which has no dp to take it from, returns it. | `PrescribedFlow(key, *, kind, dtype=torch.float64)` |
| `Quadratic`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | q = sign(dp) * 2\|dp\| / (sqrt(a^2 + 4 b \|dp\|) + a): the inverse of dp = a q + b \|q\| q, with `dp` in Pa, `a` in Pa per flow unit and `b` in Pa per flow unit squared. | `Quadratic(a, b, *, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `RegularizedPowerLaw`<br><small>also `MBLPowerLaw`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | MBL's regularised power law, ``q = C sign(dp) \|dp\|^m``, volume or mass form. | `RegularizedPowerLaw(C, m, *, dp_turbulent=0.1, form, rho_default, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `Scaled`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | F = s F_law: `law`'s flow times the dimensionless multiplier `drivers[key]`. | `Scaled(law, key)` |
| `SplineFlowTable`<br><small>also `MBLTable`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | MBL's tabulated flow law: a monotone cubic Hermite spline through ``(dp, flow)`` knots, linearly extrapolated outside them; ``flow(dp)`` always returns MASS flow in kg/s. | `SplineFlowTable(dp_points, flow_points, *, form, rho_default=None, kind='airpath')` |
| `UpstreamDensityPowerLaw`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | `PowerLaw` with `C` scaled by `(rho_upstream / rho_ref) ** m`, upstream by `sign(dp)`. | `UpstreamDensityPowerLaw(C, n, *, src, tgt, m, rho_ref=1.2041, rho_key='rho', dp_transition=0.001, regularised=None, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |

## Drives

Terms added to an edge's potential difference (stack, wind, fans).

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `DoorCompartmentHead`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | The hydrostatic part of ``DoorDiscretized.mo:64-66``, as a noodl drive: ``rho_A hAg[i] - rho_B hBg[i]`` per compartment edge, shape ``(..., n_edges)``. | `DoorCompartmentHead(kind, *, src, tgt, hAg, hBg, medium, T_key='T', Xw_key='X_w', p_key='p_abs')` |
| `ConstantDrive`<br><small>`noodl.drives`</small> | A drive that reads a pre-computed, already batched value from `drivers`. | `ConstantDrive(kind, key)` |
| `Stack`<br><small>`noodl.drives`</small> | Hydrostatic stack term (CONTAM TN 1887r1 eq. 17 with eq. 64-65 at the path elevation). | `Stack(kind, *, src, tgt, z_path, z_ref, rho_key='rho', g=9.80665)` |
| `DuctStack`<br><small>`noodl.drives`</small> | Hydrostatic term of a duct segment between two junctions: the air column at the density of the junctions' MEAN TEMPERATURE (ContamX 3.4.1.7, measured), which at one pressure is the harmonic mean of the two node densities. | `DuctStack(kind, *, src, tgt, z_ref, rho_key='rho', g=9.80665)` |
| `WindProfile`<br><small>`noodl.drives`</small> | CONTAM wind pressure profile: Cp versus relative wind angle, periodic in the angle. | `WindProfile(angles_deg, cp, *, curve='linear')` |
| `Wind`<br><small>`noodl.drives`</small> | Wind pressure on envelope paths (CONTAM TN 1887r1 section 3.15). Drivers: `rho_amb` in kg/m3, `V_met` in m/s and `theta_w` in the unit the `azimuth` edge attribute uses (degrees for networks read from CONTAM). | `Wind(kind, *, sign, envelope, azimuth, ch, cp_const, profile_index, profiles=(), rho_key='rho_amb', speed_key='V_met', direction_key='theta_w')` |

## Closures

Functions of the state that compute drivers each step (densities, flows, levels).

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `AlgebraicClosure`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | A closure that only computes drivers from the state and the drivers: called as `closure(state, drivers)`, it returns the driver entries it adds or replaces. | `AlgebraicClosure(...)` |
| `IntegratingClosure`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | A closure that advances state of its own over the step (`integrates = True`). | `IntegratingClosure(...)` |
| `ClosureSpec`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | A closure and its declarations, read once by `closure_spec`. | `ClosureSpec(closure, label, integrates, declares_integrates, state_keys, key_labels, reads, writes, edge_kinds, requires_coupling, reads_flows_of, species_columns, output_units=<factory>, owner='Model')` |

## Reactions

Transformations applied to transported species each step.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `FirstOrderDecay`<br><small>`noodl.layers`</small> | ``x <- x * exp(-rate * dt)``; ``rate`` broadcasts against ``x``. | `FirstOrderDecay(rate)` |

## Files

Readers and writers of other tools' file formats.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `write_at`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | `target` with `value` written (`add=True`: ADDED) at node `position`, in the caller's own layout (reduced `(..., n)` or stacked `(..., n, 1)`) but not necessarily its own shape: a batched `value` written into an unbatched `target` broadcasts the target up to the value's batch. Never writes into `target` itself. `where` prefixes the layout error. | `write_at(target, n, position, value, *, add=False, where='layout.write_at')` |

## Other classes

Supporting types.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `StepContext`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | What a state transition needs from the model: the interval it must integrate over (`None` under `steady()`, which an integrating closure refuses) and, when the caller tracks it, the time at the start of the step. | `StepContext(dt, t=None)` |
| `ClosureAttribute`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | One optional attribute of a closure: its name, the type it must have, what it defaults to when absent, what it means and which code consumes it. | `ClosureAttribute(name, type, default, meaning, consumer)` |
| `Field`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | A state or driver key that also knows the layout of the tensor stored under it. | `Field(key, *, role, layer, axis, labels, ordering, settable=None, n_species=1, species=None, quantity='', unit='', required='optional', default=0.0, description='', dtype=torch.float64, device='cpu', aliases=None, column=False, scalar=False)` |
| `LayerRef`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | One registered layer of a model, with its keys as discoverable `Field` attributes. | `LayerRef(name, layer, kind, *, flow_owner=None)` |
| `KeyOwnership`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | Who writes and who reads one key of a model: `writers` and `readers` are tuples of `"layer <name>"`, `"closure <label>"` or `"caller"` (the dictionary the caller gives). `field` is the key's `Field` when the model knows its layout. Closure entries come from the closure's DECLARATIONS (`inputs`, `outputs`, `state_keys`), so a closure that declares nothing is absent. | `KeyOwnership(key, field, writers, readers)` |
| `LayerRefs`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | Registered layer name -> `LayerRef`, plus the model's closure-carried keys. | `LayerRefs(model)` |
| `Issue`<br><small>`noodl.validation`</small> | One finding: `level` is `"error"`, `"warning"` or `"info"`; `key` the key concerned, if any. | `Issue(level, code, message, key=None)` |
| `InputRow`<br><small>`noodl.validation`</small> | One known key: what is expected and what was given. | `InputRow(key, role, layer, required, ordering, expected, unit, given, status)` |
| `SetupReport`<br><small>`noodl.validation`</small> | The result of `check_setup`. `ok` is true when there are no errors. | `SetupReport(issues=<factory>, rows=<factory>, probed=False, driver_reads=frozenset(), state_reads=frozenset(), closure_outputs=frozenset())` |
| `UndefinedSteadyState`<br><small>`noodl.layers`</small> | A steady transport solve has no answer: a stored node keeps everything that enters it (nothing leaves it, or it belongs to a closed group whose contents never reach a boundary outflow, a removal or a filter loss). A `ValueError`, raised before the solve and naming the nodes; `layer` is the layer's name and `nodes` the nodes refused. | `UndefinedSteadyState(message, *, layer, nodes)` |
| `AirMedium`<br><small>also `MBLMedium`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | An air medium's default state and the two densities its flow elements need. | `AirMedium(name, p_default, T_default, X_default, rho_default, has_moisture, _buoyancy, _density=None, _cp=None)` |
| `LawContext`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | What a dynamic or implicit constitutive law needs besides its own edge values. | `LawContext(mode, dt=None, t=None, integration='trapezoidal', dp_prev=None, q_prev=None, omega=None)` |
| `SplineCurve`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | A measured curve y(x) fitted as ContamX fits it (see the module docstring). | `SplineCurve(x, y, *, name='')` |
| `Conversion`<br><small>`noodl.couple`</small> | One registered conversion and the UNITS it maps between, `(from_unit, to_unit, fn)`. | `Conversion(from_unit, to_unit, fn)` |
| `ValueLink`<br><small>`noodl.couple`</small> | One shared-node value relationship. | `ValueLink(from_model, from_key, from_index, to_model, to_key, to_index=0, convert=None, two_way=False, convert_back=None, sources_key=None)` |
| `DriverAlias`<br><small>`noodl.couple`</small> | One driver value shared across models: `source` is authoritative; every target is overwritten from it through that target's own registered conversion (or none). | `DriverAlias(source, targets)` |

## Functions

Calculations and helpers.

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `closure_spec`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | Read `closure`'s declarations into a `ClosureSpec`: the only reader of the closure attributes (`CLOSURE_ATTRIBUTES`). `index` is the closure's position, for the message about a non-callable; `owner` prefixes every message. | `closure_spec(closure, *, index, owner='Model')` |
| `call_closure`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | Call a closure (or its `ClosureSpec`) by the one dispatch rule: three arguments for an integrating closure, two otherwise. For callers outside `Model` that run a closure themselves; a bare closure is read with `closure_spec` first. | `call_closure(closure_or_spec, state, drivers, ctx=None)` |
| `reaction_species_columns`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | A `Reaction`'s optional `species_columns` (the same member as a closure's), `{}` when it declares none. `TypeError` if malformed. | `reaction_species_columns(reaction)` |
| `check_species_columns`<br><small>`noodl.contracts`</small> | Raise `ValueError` unless every `{layer: {name: column}}` in `declared` names a transport layer of `transport`, has `column < n_species`, and, when the layer has `species_names`, `species_names[column] == name`. A layer without `species_names` cannot verify names, so it accepts only declarations that give distinct columns. `label` names the closure or reaction in the message. | `check_species_columns(label, declared, transport)` |
| `batch_shape`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | The batch shape of `x`: its shape without its last `n_trailing` physical dimensions. `ValueError` if `x` has fewer dimensions than that. | `batch_shape(x, n_trailing)` |
| `broadcast_batch`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | Broadcast the batch shapes of `items`, each `(tensor, number of trailing physical dims)`. Returns the common batch shape and every tensor `.expand()`-ed to that batch plus its own trailing shape (views, no copies). The batch is aligned on the LEFT of the physical axes, never against them, so a batch of size `n` cannot be mistaken for a node axis. `RuntimeError` naming the shapes if the batches do not broadcast. | `broadcast_batch(*items)` |
| `per_instance`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | A float, or a tensor with one value per instance `(B...)`, as `(B..., 1, ...)` with `n_trailing` trailing singleton axes, in `like`'s dtype and device. It then broadcasts against `like` `(B..., physical...)` over the batch only, never against a physical axis (a batch of size `n` is not a node axis). `RuntimeError` if its batch does not broadcast with `like`'s. | `per_instance(value, like, n_trailing)` |
| `is_stacked`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | True when `x` is in STACKED layout `(..., n, K)`: at least `min_dim` dimensions (never fewer than 2) and trailing shape `(n, K)`. With `K == 1` this is the `(..., n, 1)` column, as opposed to the reduced `(..., n)`. | `is_stacked(x, n, K=1, *, min_dim=2)` |
| `as_stacked`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | `(x as (..., n, K), reduced?)` by the one rule: stacked `(..., n, K)` first; for `K == 1` also reduced `(..., n)`, returned with a trailing axis and `reduced=True`. `min_dim` is the fewest dimensions of the stacked form (the reduced form needs one fewer): 3 where the leading axis is time. `ValueError("{where}: {name!r} must be ...")` otherwise. | `as_stacked(x, n, K, *, name, where, min_dim=2)` |
| `as_layout`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | `x_stacked` `(..., n, 1)` back in the caller's layout: `(..., n)` if `reduced`, unchanged otherwise (the inverse of `as_stacked` for one species). | `as_layout(x_stacked, reduced)` |
| `reduced_single`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | A single-species tensor in REDUCED layout `(..., n)`, whether it came stacked `(..., n, 1)` or reduced. A batched `(1, 1)` is both and holds one number, so the ambiguity at `n == 1` is harmless. `ValueError("{where}: ...")` if its last axis is not `n` entries. | `reduced_single(x, n, *, where)` |
| `species_columns`<br><small>`noodl.layout`</small> | The column of each `wanted` species name in the `declared` order (a layer's `species_names`). `order="any"` allows a subset in any order; `order="exact"` requires `wanted == declared`. Unknown and repeated names raise `ValueError`, naming them, with `where` as prefix. With `declared=None` (the layer names no species) the names cannot be resolved: the identity `[0, 1, ...]` is returned, only when `len(wanted) == n_species`. | `species_columns(declared, wanted, *, where, n_species=None, order='any')` |
| `normalize_unit`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | A unit string in one canonical spelling, for comparison only (this is not a units library: nothing is converted, and two different units never compare equal). | `normalize_unit(unit)` |
| `units_agree`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | Whether two unit strings are the same unit up to `normalize_unit`'s spellings. | `units_agree(a, b)` |
| `input_field`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | A `Field` for an input a closure, reaction, law or drive reads itself (a wind speed, an inflow), as a closure's `input_specs` or a builder's `model.input_specs` declares it. | `input_field(model, key, *, description, unit='', over=None, required=True, ordering=None)` |
| `input_unit_declarations`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | `(origin, key, unit)` for every input a model, closure or reaction declares in `input_specs`, in declaration order; `unit` is `""` when the spec gives none. `origin` names the declarer (`"model"`, a closure's or reaction's `repr`). | `input_unit_declarations(model)` |
| `required_state_keys`<br><small>`noodl.refs`</small> | The state keys `Model.step` reads from the step-start state. | `required_state_keys(model)` |
| `active_interior`<br><small>`noodl.layers`</small> | Split the non-boundary nodes of `net` into the ones `kinds` touch and the ones it does not: `(interior_idx, inactive_idx)`, both in NODE order, both excluding `boundary`. | `active_interior(net, kinds, boundary)` |
| `Orifice`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | PowerLaw(C = Cd * A * sqrt(2 / rho), n = 0.5): the sharp-edged orifice equation, as a VOLUME flow in m3/s from `Cd` (dimensionless discharge coefficient), `A` (m2) and `rho` (kg/m3). | `Orifice(Cd, A, *, rho=1.2, dp_transition=0.001, regularised=None, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `air_viscosity`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Dynamic viscosity of air (Pa s) at temperature `T` (K): ContamX's linear law, 1.81625e-5 + 4.92859e-8 (T - 293.15), measured between 253 and 333 K. | `air_viscosity(T)` |
| `discretized_door`<br><small>also `mbl_discretized_door`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | One ``DoorDiscretizedOpen`` as ``nCom`` edges of ``kind``: the compartment element and its head drive. Defaults are MBL's (``DoorDiscretized.mo:6-11``, ``TwoWayFlowElementBuoyancy.mo:6-14``, ``DoorDiscretizedOpen.mo:6``, ``TwoWayFlowElement.mo:19``). ``dA = wOpe hOpe / nCom`` on every edge (``DoorDiscretizedOpen.mo:23``, ``DoorDiscretized.mo:60``). | `discretized_door(*, src, tgt, medium, nCom=10, wOpe=0.9, hOpe=2.1, hA=1.35, hB=1.35, CD=0.65, m=0.5, dp_turbulent=0.01, vZer=0.001, kind='door', T_key='T', Xw_key='X_w', p_key='p_abs')` |
| `discretized_operable_door`<br><small>also `mbl_discretized_operable_door`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | One ``DoorDiscretizedOperable`` as ``nCom`` edges of ``kind``; see :func:`discretized_door`. ``AOpe = wOpe hOpe`` (``DoorDiscretizedOperable.mo:35``); ``LClo`` has no MBL default. | `discretized_operable_door(*, src, tgt, medium, y_key, LClo, nCom=10, wOpe=0.9, hOpe=2.1, hA=1.35, hB=1.35, CDOpe=0.65, CDClo=0.65, CDCloRat=1.0, dpCloRat=4.0, mOpe=0.5, mClo=0.65, dp_turbulent=0.01, vZer=0.001, kind='door', T_key='T', Xw_key='X_w', p_key='p_abs')` |
| `effective_leakage_area`<br><small>also `mbl_ela`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | ``EffectiveAirLeakageArea.mo:3-5,7-14,16``: ``C = L * CDRat * sqrt(2 / rho_default) * dpRat ** (0.5 - m)``, ``m = 0.65`` by default (``:4``), ``dpRat = 4`` Pa (``:7-9``), ``CDRat = 1`` (``:11-14``). | `effective_leakage_area(L, dpRat=4.0, CDRat=1.0, m=0.65, dp_turbulent=0.1, *, rho_default, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `medium`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Look up one of the three air media, by physical name or by Modelica class path. | `medium(name)` |
| `open_door_pair`<br><small>also `mbl_door_pair`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Both edges of one ``DoorOpen`` (or of several, with per-door ``src``/``tgt``): the ``"ab"`` edge (path 1) with kind ``f"{kind}_ab"`` and the ``"ba"`` edge (path 2) with kind ``f"{kind}_ba"``, sharing every keyword argument of :class:`OpenDoor`. | `open_door_pair(*, kind='door', **kwargs)` |
| `operable_door_pair`<br><small>also `mbl_operable_door_pair`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Both edges of one ``DoorOperable``; see :func:`open_door_pair`. | `operable_door_pair(*, kind='door', **kwargs)` |
| `power_law_coefficient`<br><small>also `mbl_coefficient`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | ``Coefficient_V_flow.mo``/``Coefficient_m_flow.mo``: ``C``/``k`` and ``m`` given directly, with no further formula -- a direct pass-through to :class:`RegularizedPowerLaw`. | `power_law_coefficient(C, m, form, dp_turbulent=0.1, *, rho_default, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `power_law_from_point`<br><small>also `mbl_point`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | ``Point_m_flow.mo:4-5``: ``k = mMea_flow_nominal / dpMea_nominal ** m``, fit from one measured (dp, m_flow) pair; ``m`` stays a free parameter (default 0.5, inherited from ``Coefficient_m_flow``'s ``PowerLawResistanceParameters(m=0.5)``, ``Coefficient_m_flow.mo:27-28``). | `power_law_from_point(dpMea, mMea_flow, m=0.5, dp_turbulent=0.1, *, rho_default, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `power_law_from_points`<br><small>also `mbl_points`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | ``Points_m_flow.mo:4-6,15-16``: the flow exponent itself is derived from two measured (dp, m_flow) pairs, ``m = (ln(mMea[0]) - ln(mMea[1])) / (ln(dpMea[0]) - ln(dpMea[1]))``, then ``k = mMea[0] / dpMea[0] ** m``. ``dpMea``/``mMea_flow`` are each a 2-element sequence. | `power_law_from_points(dpMea, mMea_flow, dp_turbulent=0.1, *, rho_default, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `regularized_orifice`<br><small>also `mbl_orifice`</small><br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | ``Orifice.mo:3-5,9``: ``C = CD * A * sqrt(2 / rho_default)``, ``m = 0.5`` by default (overridable, per ``Orifice.mo:3``'s non-``final`` ``m=0.5`` modifier); ``C`` itself is ``final`` in MBL (does not depend on ``m``). ``CD`` defaults to 0.65 (``Orifice.mo:9``, the sharp-edged-orifice discharge coefficient). | `regularized_orifice(A, CD=0.65, m=0.5, dp_turbulent=0.1, *, rho_default, kind='airpath', learnable=False)` |
| `check_drive_signature`<br><small>`noodl.drives`</small> | Raise `TypeError` unless `drive` is callable as `drive(drivers)`. | `check_drive_signature(drive, *, where)` |
| `apply_conversion`<br><small>`noodl.couple`</small> | `value` unchanged if `name` is None; the registered conversion otherwise. | `apply_conversion(name, value, drivers)` |
| `transport_boundary_inflow`<br><small>`noodl.couple`</small> | Net mass INFLOW, `(...,)`, at the boundary node `boundary_idx[node_position]`, in a transport layer's own units, for a SINGLE-SPECIES layer (`x_interior`/`x_boundary` are `(..., n_i)`/`(..., n_b)`, never `(..., n_i, K)`). | `transport_boundary_inflow(net, q, flow_kinds, x_interior, x_boundary, interior_idx, boundary_idx, node_position)` |
| `union`<br><small>`noodl.couple`</small> | Couple `models` by exchanging the driver/state values `shared` names, WITHOUT merging any model's `Network`, layers, or closures. Never modifies the `Model`/`State`/`Drivers` objects passed in -- returns fresh dict copies. | `union(models, shared, *, substeps=None, relaxation=0.5, iterate_rtol=1e-08, iterate_atol=0.0, iterate_max=50, adjoint_rtol=1e-10)` |

## Constants and tables

Named values and option tables.

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| `CLOSURE_ATTRIBUTES` | `tuple` |

## Base classes (for extending)

Subclass these to add a constitutive law, drive, closure, reaction or node source; see [Extending noodl](../development/extending.md).

| Name | What it does | How to call it |
|---|---|---|
| `Reaction`<br><small>`noodl.layers`</small> | A local, per-node nonlinear map applied to the state after a transport step (or before it, under `Model(reaction_order="before_transport")`). | `Reaction(...)` |
| `ConstitutiveLaw`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | Abstract branch law: flow as a function of potential difference. | `ConstitutiveLaw(kind)` |
| `ImplicitLaw`<br><small>`noodl.elements`</small> | A constitutive law written as a relation `residual(dp, q, drivers, ctx) = 0`. | `ImplicitLaw(kind)` |
| `Drive`<br><small>`noodl.drives`</small> | A drive must read every differentiable quantity from `drivers`, never own one. | `Drive(...)` |
| `NodeSource`<br><small>`noodl.nodesources`</small> | Base class: a potential-dependent withdrawal at a fixed set of nodes. | `NodeSource(nodes)` |
